prompt:
You are a senior typographer and information designer. You lay out data tables for publication. You judge layouts by looking at the rendered result as a whole: what the table is for, how a reader scans and compares it, which columns belong together or play the same role, proportion and rhythm across columns, a clear hierarchy of headers and groups, whether rows read as units, whether words, numbers and identifiers stay intact, and how text and white space are distributed. Fewer lines or a shorter table is not automatically better, and neither is equal widths or symmetry; decide case by case and say why.

Table: مواقيت الصلاة في مدن سعودية (language ar, right-to-left: column 1 is on the RIGHT).
Grid: 6 columns × 7 rows. Row headers: yes (first logical column identifies each row).
Per-column content facts (content px at 15px font, excluding padding):
  col 1: header "المدينة" · longest unbreakable word 49px · one-line width 91px
  col 2: header "الفجر" · longest unbreakable word 35px · one-line width 35px
  col 3: header "الظهر" · longest unbreakable word 35px · one-line width 35px
  col 4: header "العصر" · longest unbreakable word 38px · one-line width 38px
  col 5: header "المغرب" · longest unbreakable word 47px · one-line width 47px
  col 6: header "العشاء" · longest unbreakable word 41px · one-line width 41px
Each column also has 21px of padding+border, so a column given width w px shows w−21 px of text.
Available width: 414px (the dashed pink box). The column widths you choose must sum to at most 413px.
Fixed: content, font, 15px font size, padding, borders, colours, alignment. You control ONLY the column widths.

The image shows the table's content with every cell on one line, so you can read everything. Study it first.
1) Understand it: what is the table for, how will people read, scan and compare it, which columns play the same or similar role, which values must stay intact, which text may wrap naturally, and where existing row height could absorb wrapping.
2) Propose 3 genuinely different column-width designs for 414px (different strategies, not small variations).
Reply ONLY JSON: {"understanding":{"purpose":"","reading":"","groups":["columns that belong together and why"],"keep_intact":[""],"may_wrap":[""]},"designs":[{"name":"A","widths":[int px per column, column 1 first],"idea":"one sentence"}]}

log.raw: {"understanding":{"purpose":"A quick-reference timetable of daily prayer times for six Saudi cities: readers look up one city's day, or compare one prayer across cities.","reading":"Right-to-left: the eye lands on the city name (row header) first, then sweeps left across the five prayer times; the dominant comparison is column-wise (same prayer across cities), with row-wise reading as the secondary mode.","groups":["col 1 (المدينة) is the row identifier and must be visually separated from the data block","cols 2–6 (الفجر، الظهر، العصر، المغرب، العشاء) are five instances of the same kind of value — clock times — and should read as one uniform band, with no column appearing more important than another"],"keep_intact":["every time value, e.g. 8:16, 12:24, 3:23 — they must never wrap or break at the colon","the single-word headers الفجر، الظهر، العصر، المغرب، العشاء, which cannot wrap and set each column's minimum width"],"may_wrap":["city names, especially المدينة المنورة (two words) and مكة المكرمة — wrapping them to a second line is harmless because the row height already accommodates two lines"]},"designs":[{"name":"A","widths":[73,68,68,68,68,68],"idea":"Democratic grid: one narrow row-header column that lets long city names wrap, and five identical time columns so no prayer looks more important than another."},{"name":"B","widths":[112,56,56,59,68,62],"idea":"City-first: spend almost all slack on a wide row header that keeps every city on one line, and squeeze each time column to its exact header minimum."},{"name":"C","widths":[91,60,60,62,70,70],"idea":"Two-tier: a one-line city column at its natural width, tight columns for the three daytime prayers, and slightly airier columns for the evening pair (المغرب، العشاء) that close the row."}]}
